claims.text: The alloy has nominal composition Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Vacuum-arc melting, homogenization at 1200 °C, hot forging, re-homogenization at 1200 °C, and water quenching yield a high-temperature disordered BCC state.
Rapid cooling causes spinodal decomposition of the disordered BCC phase.
Spinodal decomposition separates the BCC phase into Ni–Al-lean and Ni–Al-rich regions.
Below an ordering transition, the Ni–Al-rich regions order into B2 precipitates.
The resulting structure is a hierarchical Ni–Al-lean BCC matrix containing Ni–Al-rich ordered B2 precipitates.
Larger B2 particles may contain embedded Ni–Al-lean BCC nanoparticles.
Minor FCC phases coexist with the hierarchical BCC/B2 microstructure.
The hierarchical BCC/B2 microstructure impedes dislocation motion.
The 1100 °C annealed-and-quenched condition has a nearly equal BCC/FCC phase mixture.
The 1100 °C condition has lower hardness than the 1200 and 1300 °C conditions.
Quenching from 1200 and 1300 °C produces a larger overall BCC fraction than quenching from 1100 °C.
Quenching from 1200 and 1300 °C produces more pronounced spinodal decomposition than quenching from 1100 °C.
Quenching from 1200 and 1300 °C produces a greater density of B2 precipitates than quenching from 1100 °C.
Quenching from 1200 and 1300 °C produces a finer distribution of B2 precipitates than quenching from 1100 °C.
The 1200 and 1300 °C conditions have higher Rockwell C hardness than the 1100 °C condition.
Significantly different cooling rates may change the proposed phase-stability behavior.

contradictions.description: The material_initial_state says water quenching yields a disordered BCC state, whereas the hypothesis says rapid cooling drives that state through spinodal decomposition and B2 ordering. Without distinguishing separate quench histories or quench-rate windows, the claimed post-quench initial state and the claimed transformations during quenching are inconsistent.

The structural mediator describes FCC as minor, while the 1100 °C baseline is described as a nearly equal BCC/FCC mixture. The mediator is not explicitly restricted to the higher-temperature conditions, creating a cross-field inconsistency in the stated FCC fraction.
